articles.headline: Deep Grid Surges Define Phoenix as Hildebrand and Denley Carve Forward
articles.dek: Traffic management on the flat mile created divergent paths through the field during the General Tire 150.
articles.body:
Passing at Phoenix Raceway usually demands patience on the bottom groove, but Friday's General Tire 150 rewarded drivers who committed to deep-field charges. With four caution periods breaking up green-flag runs, track position shifted repeatedly between long-run pace and restart execution.

Sekani Hildebrand authored the clearest example of that movement. Starting 24th in the 30-car field, the driver of the No. 40 car advanced 21 positions over 200 circuits, ultimately leading 22 laps on the way to a third-place result. Hildebrand reached the front pack without relying entirely on pit strategy, utilizing short-run speed to pick off cars off Turn 2 before settling into the top five during the second half of the event.

## Denley Follows Similar Route

Alfie Denley executed a parallel climb. Grid position 27 gave the No. 97 team little room to maneuver early, yet Denley picked up 21 spots to finish sixth. Denley also led 11 laps during the middle stages, showing that long-run setups could overcome poor qualifying efforts on the flat mile.

Further back, Julius Paxton gained 15 positions, moving from 26th on the grid to cross the line 11th. Jason Smith similarly recovered from the 30th starting spot to place 13th without pacing any laps.

## Trouble for Front Row Starters

The ability to move forward contrasted sharply with the struggles of several drivers who began near the front. Pole sitter Caleb Guerrier failed to lead a single circuit in the No. 06, drifting back into traffic and crossing the line ninth. While Guerrier preserved a top-ten result, the lack of front-running pace left him exposed on restarts.

Mechanical issues also removed several contenders prematurely. Tyler Raheem and Caden Everett both retired due to engine failures, while Vincent Crook parked with suspension damage. A late accident eliminated Kolby Newman, holding the attrition count to four cars.

At the front, William Faison held off Daniel Stavchansky by 0.687 seconds after controlling 95 circuits. Yet behind that duel, the movement through the midpack showed that grid position meant very little once the tires aged on the abrasive surface. Hildebrand and Denley proved that starting deep did not prohibit leading laps or securing high finishes, setting a standard for field navigation that will face a completely different test when the tour travels to Kansas Speedway in April.
articles.author: Priya Nandakumar

articles.headline: William Faison Captures General Tire 150 Victory at Phoenix Raceway
articles.dek: William Faison drove to victory lane at Phoenix Raceway after leading 95 laps in the second race of the ARCA Menards Series season.
articles.body:
William Faison secured the win in the General Tire 150 at Phoenix Raceway, holding off Daniel Stavchanksy by 0.687 seconds at the finish line. Faison started second on the grid in the 30-car field and dominated the flat, unique layout by pacing the pack for 95 circuits. The victory vaults Faison directly into the championship conversation after two rounds of the 20-race season.

Daniel Stavchanksy finished second after starting fifth and leading 27 laps, maintaining his hold on the top spot in the driver standings. Sekani Hildebrand delivered the performance of the day by charging from his 24th starting position all the way to third, also spending 22 laps at the front of the field. John Verstappen and Karson Mitchell rounded out the top five positions, with both drivers leading 12 laps apiece during the 200-lap event.

The race featured four cautions that slowed the pace and mixed up strategies across the field. Attrition played a role as four drivers failed to finish, including Caden Everett and Tyler Raheem due to engine failures, Kolby Newman to an accident, and Vincent Crook with suspension issues. Pole sitter Caleb Guerrier dropped back from the front row starting spot to finish ninth without leading a lap.

In the early season standings, Daniel Stavchanksy leads with 360 points and one win, followed closely by William Faison with 355 points and one win. John Verstappen and Karson Mitchell sit tied for third with 325 points each, while James Baker holds fifth with 322 points.

The ARCA Menards Series continues its opening stretch next week as the sim drivers prepare for the third round of the 2027 schedule.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: Faison Field Surge Highlights Daytona Opener Numbers
articles.dek: A detailed look at the statistics behind William Faison charging from the back of the pack at Daytona.
articles.body:
Opening weekend at Daytona International Speedway brought 188 laps of intense superspeedway racing for the ARCA Menards Series field. Thirty cars took the green flag on February 14, and the attrition rate showed right away with five cautions slowing the pace.

While Daniel Stavchansky grabbed the headlines and the trophy by leading 78 laps from the eighth starting spot, the statistical standout of the afternoon was William Faison. Starting dead last in 29th position, Faison picked his way through the draft and survived the multi-car incidents that eliminated drivers like Scott Chegg and Tyler Raheem.

Faison managed to lead 18 laps during the afternoon before crossing the stripe in third place behind Stavchansky and runner-up James Baker. That massive 26-spot gain earned Faison the biggest mover honors of the event and propelled him to third in the early season standings with 170 points.

Karson Mitchell also showed immediate speed by putting his machine on the pole and leading 16 laps before settling for fourth. John Verstappen rounded out the top five after starting eleventh and pacing the field for 14 circuits.

Attention now turns away from the superspeedways as the series prepares for the General Tire 150 at Phoenix Raceway on March 5.

articles.headline: Stavchansky Outduels Baker to Win Daytona ARCA Opener
articles.dek: Daniel Stavchansky kicked off the 2027 ARCA Menards Series season with a commanding victory at Daytona International Speedway after leading 78 laps.
articles.body:
Daniel Stavchansky started the 2027 sim-racing season in dominant fashion, capturing the General Tire 200 victory at Daytona International Speedway on Saturday. Stavchansky guided his number 03 machine to the front and stayed there, pacing the 30-car field for 78 of the 188 scheduled laps in the opening round of the twenty-race schedule.

James Baker applied heavy pressure in the closing laps but crossed the finish line 0.873 seconds behind the winner to secure second place. William Faison delivered the drive of the day, carving his way through traffic from the 29th starting position to finish third. Pole sitter Karson Mitchell led 16 laps early on before settling for fourth, while John Verstappen rounded out the top five after leading 14 circuits.

The 188-lap superspeedway opener featured five caution periods that mixed up the pack and triggered heavy attrition near the rear of the field. Mechanical failures and on-track incidents eliminated drivers such as Scott Chegg, Tyler Raheem, Kolby Newman, Valdemar Estriden, and Vincent Crook before the checkered flag waved.

In the early season standings, Stavchansky leads the field with 185 points. Baker sits second with 175 points, followed by Faison with 170, Mitchell with 165, and Verstappen with 160.

The ARCA Menards Series continues its 20-race calendar with the second round of the season scheduled at the next track on the tour.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

interviews.quote: Starting back in twenty-fourth makes you work for every single position. The crew gave me a great setup to slice through the traffic.
Our car was hooked up all day long. Once we got to the front, we just had to manage the tires and hit our marks.
Starting back in 29th makes you work for it. The guys gave me a fast car and we just picked them off one by one.
We gave it everything at the end. Second is a solid points day to start the year, but we wanted that trophy.
Our car was hooked up all afternoon. We just had to hit our marks and keep the draft working for us.

chase.headline: Final Ledger Locked
chase.summary: All twenty races are complete in the simulation, leaving Daniel Stavchanksy on top with 2986 points. Tyler Payne and Caleb Guerrier round out the final podium positions cleanly.

notes.daniel stavchanksy: Secured the top spot with 2986 points backed by a recent win at the JR and CO 150.
notes.tyler payne: Finished second overall on 2958 points following a victory at the Spruce 212.
notes.caleb guerrier: Claimed third in the standings with 2951 points after taking the checkered flag at the Bushs Beans 200.

race.headline: Offseason Silence
race.summary: The schedule is entirely finished with zero events remaining on the calendar. Drivers are resting up while the garage packs away the tools until next year.

notes.john verstappen: Wrapped up his campaign holding a 68 reputation after charging from twenty-third to second at the Menards 150.
notes.william faison: Closed out the year with a 71 reputation following a strong run from twenty-ninth to fifth at the Bushs Beans 200.
notes.king robinson: Finished his season with a 73 reputation after moving from twenty-seventh to ninth at Watkins Glen.

season.headline: The Books Are Closed
season.summary: Another full twenty-race slate is officially in the rear-view mirror. Stavchanksy proved untouchable over the long haul while the rest of the field fought for scraps.

notes.daniel stavchanksy: Proved to be the class of the field all year long to capture the simulated championship.
notes.tyler payne: Put together a solid runner-up campaign but had to settle for second best in the final tally.
notes.julius paxton: Rounded out the top tier in twenty-second position with 2164 points.
